title: Veterinary nurse (RCVS)
overviewOfRole: Provides individualised care for animals in a vet practice or animal hospital working collaboratively as part of a team and with vet surgeons.
entryRequirements: <p>Learners must evidence capability in numeracy, literacy and science, written and spoken English and mathematics. This would typically include GCSEs at grades 9 to 4 (or A* to C), including English, mathematics and a science subject or equivalent.</p>

knowledges.detail: The RCVS Day One Competences for Veterinary Nurses.
The RCVS Code of Professional Conduct and its associated guidance.
Organisational requirements and legislation related to a veterinary business and animal welfare.
Effective health and safety within a veterinary practice.
Anatomy and physiology in relation to veterinary nursing practice.
Normal form and function of body systems.
The relationship between normal form and function and the effect of disease processes and the consequent nursing requirements of sick animals.
The role of infection in animal and human health.
The principles of disease transmission.
The principles of disinfection and sterilisation.
How to maintain personal hygiene especially in relation to cross-infection.
The principles of infection monitoring and control.
Correct usage, handling, storage, maintenance and disposal materials, equipment and instruments.
The principles of record keeping.
The principles of medical veterinary nursing and support.
The principles of surgical veterinary nursing and support including anaesthesia.
The principles of safe and responsible pharmacology to include administration of medication and usage, handling and disposal of veterinary pharmaceuticals.
The principles of first aid.
The principles of nursing support and the triage, stabilisation and treatment of emergency patients.
Nursing requirements of critically ill or injured animals.
Intensive nursing care techniques and requirements for veterinary patients.
The principles of radiography and imaging techniques.
The principles of how to take and process radiographs.
The principles of how to manage and store diagnostic images.
The function and use of a range of laboratory equipment.
The principles of how to prepare specimens for transportation.
The principles of how to collect, prepare, test pathological samples.
The principles and methods of effective communication and their impact on clients and patient care.
Factors affecting working relationships with clients and within the veterinary team.
The principles relating to evidence based approaches to personal development and practice.
Personal and professional limitations.
How to seek and use feedback and advice.
The principles of efficient workflow and time management.

behaviours.detail: Works co-operatively and collaboratively, promoting equity, diversity, belonging, civility and inclusion.
Commits to the process of reflection, and continuous learning and professional development.
Acts in a professional, ethical manner, recognising professional and personal requirements and limitations.
Demonstrates compliance with the RCVS regulatory requirements to prioritise animal welfare and wellbeing of people.
Upholds and contributes positively to the reputation of the profession.
Practises in line with best available evidence with a commitment to evidence-based improvement and enhancement.

skills.detail: Demonstrates RCVS day one skills.
Prepare and maintain a sustainable working environment in accordance with current legislation, regulations, wellbeing policies, manufacturers guidelines and standard operating procedures.
Critically assess hazards and minimise risks in the working environment.
Create, maintain, and store clinical records and manage the use of personal data in accordance with current legislation and practice policy.
Communicate with internal and external stakeholders, maintaining civility and empathy using a variety of methods and styles.
Communicate patient status and care requirements to veterinary care team and clients.
Handle and restrain animals ethically and safely.
Practise evidence based nursing care in accordance with practice policy and standard operating procedures.
Devise, implement and critically evaluate nursing care strategies in collaboration with the veterinary care team and clients.
Plan diagnostic procedure strategies in collaboration with the veterinary team.
Obtain and process laboratory samples and diagnostic images in accordance with current legislation, regulation, practice policy and standard operating procedures.
Handle, manage, dispense, store and dispose of pharmaceuticals sustainably in accordance with current legislation, regulation and practice policy and procedures.
Administer medicines prescribed by the veterinary surgeon and in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.
Formulate and implement sustainable biosecurity strategies.
Plan sustainable surgical and non-surgical procedure strategies in collaboration with the veterinary team.
Prepare and position patients for surgical and non-surgical procedures in accordance with the strategic plan.
Assist the veterinary team with surgical and non-surgical procedures in accordance with the strategic plan.
Utilise checklists to maximise patient safety and minimise risk.
Plan sustainable anaesthesia strategies in collaboration with the veterinary team.
Prepare, position, monitor and maintain patients for anaesthesia in accordance with the strategic plan.
Formulate, reflect on and implement auditing and quality improvement strategies.
Formulate, reflect on and implement practice protocols which consider the health, safety and wellbeing of both the individual and wider team.

qualifications.title: A level 3 diploma in veterinary nursing that is accredited by the RCVS as a “licence to practise” in veterinary nursing, and which entitle holders to apply to enter the RCVS Register of Veterinary Nurses.
qualifications.anyAdditionalInformation: Please refer to the Awarding Organisation to confirm if English and maths is an essential component of any mandatory qualification.

duties.dutyDetail: Keep up to date with legislation affecting practice.
Communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders.
Take samples and perform laboratory tests and procedures.
Prepare, maintain and assist theatre practices.
Prepare, support, maintain and monitor anaesthesia.
